title: NEAR Shoemaker on Eros
gravity_note: Eros's gravity is about 1/2000 of Earth's. A jump would keep you floating for minutes, and a really hard one could throw you off Eros for good (escape speed is only about 10 m/s).

note: Landing site 37.2 S, 81.6 E (IAU planetocentric; = 278.4 W in the NEAR catalog convention), just south of the Himeros saddle; touchdown 2001-02-12. Source: PDS SBN "NEAR Coordinate Systems" document. "Up" is the normal of the best-fit plane of the terrain within 500 m of the site; "north" (row 0 side) is the Eros spin axis projected onto that plane. The shape model has a vertex spacing of about 25-30 m, so it does not resolve boulders or spacecraft-sized features; the 3.9 m grid is interpolated from the facets. Colour is shaded relief rendered from the shape model (sun from the north-west), not a photograph; the shape model has no albedo, so brightness only shows slopes. Heights smoothed with a 25 m Gaussian to hide plate facets.
